items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The musicians other than Frank Newton that I did not know were Dickie Wells, trombone... I was with a bunch of musicians... Dickie Wells, Mack Walker, Harold McFerran, John William and myself ate in restaurants.

ctx.x: his brother Cecil who stood in front of the orchestra with a top hat on his head like Ted Lewis. That was the most money I had ever made in one night and I never thought that Lloyd had cheated me out of anything if he took a bigger cut from the percentage because he had the responsibility of transportation and other things. I never expected to find another leader like Clarence Paige who counted the money out in packages of ten and gave everyone the same amount from a percentage dance and then asked everyone for…

But I was so happy about the money I received from Lloyd Scott after the first job I did with the group that I saw myself having a bankroll large enough to choke an elephant in a few days. The next job we did, I received $ 7.00 but that was not at all bad for those days. My bankroll did not grow as I thought it would after the first night's pay, but I was happy because I was with a bunch of musicians that had been some places and had musical ideas that I had not experienced before. The musicians other than Frank…

The Scott brothers and Don Frie were born in Springfield, Ohio, Dickie Wells, Harold McFerran and Mack Walker came from Louisville, Ky., Frank Newton was from Virginia and Hubert Mann from West Virginia. (Harold McFerran and Mack Walker were half-brothers).

items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I recorded with Dicky Wells' Orchestra... Dicky and I did three other numbers... I played this session with Dicky Wells... I was happy playing with my ole buddy Dickie Wells

ctx.x: Teddy had changed a few musicians since I left the band in 1935. Bob Carroll, ex-Redman alumnus, was on tenor, having replaced Chu Berry; Wilbur de Paris had been added on trombone, and a young 18-year old trumpet played named John Burks Gillespie whom the other fellows in the band called Dizzy. Dizzy had replaced Frank Newton who had come in the band after I left.

My recording activities started the 7th of July when I recorded with Dicky Wells' Orchestra which included Bill Dillard, Shad Collins, who had replaced Roy Eldridge, Dicky, Django Reinhardt, Richard Fullbright on bass and Bill Beeson on drums.
